topic: Events after the balance sheet date
question: Explain the accounting treatment of events occurring after the balance sheet date under AS 4 'Contingencies and Events Occurring after the Balance Sheet Date'.
sources: AS 4 Contingencies and Events Occurring after the Balance Sheet Date (as revised)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Significant events, favourable or unfavourable, that occur between the balance sheet date and the date on which the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors (or other approving authority).
points.basis: AS 4, definition of events occurring after the balance sheet date

points.label: Adjusting events
points.description: Events that give more evidence about conditions existing at the balance sheet date require the assets and liabilities to be adjusted, e.g. insolvency of a debtor that existed at the year end.

points.label: Non-adjusting events
points.description: Events that relate to conditions arising after the balance sheet date are not adjusted, but if material they are disclosed in the report of the approving authority with their nature and an estimate of the financial effect (or a statement that it cannot be estimated).
points.basis: AS 4, events not requiring adjustment and their disclosure

points.label: Going concern
points.description: Assets and liabilities are adjusted for events after the balance sheet date that show the going concern assumption is no longer appropriate for the whole or part of the enterprise.
points.basis: AS 4, events affecting the going concern assumption

points.label: Proposed dividend
points.description: Dividends proposed or declared after the balance sheet date are not recognised as a liability at the balance sheet date; they are disclosed in the notes.
points.basis: AS 4 (as revised), treatment of dividends proposed after the balance sheet date
